work.agent_query: Read AGENT_TASK.md and docs/INTERFACE.md. Integrate ALFWorld into the supplied Miles checkout (repo/) and task_entry.py so that Qwen3-4B is trained with GRPO on multi-turn ALFWorld episodes, following the rendering, workload and loss contract exactly and keeping it a Miles training job (Megatron-Core inside Miles' training actor, SGLang engines started by Miles, the same implementation for probe and run), then maximize the score: the hidden-set success the complete training run adds to the policy, in percentage points, per hour of timed training (0 below a 15-point gain), so a faster run and a policy that learns more both count. Use the public suites (python /opt/miles_alfworld_public/run_public.py, suites cpu, probe, small, perf; outputs under /scratch) only to get the pipeline working and passing its checks. They are far smaller than the scored run and do not predict the score: think about how your pipeline behaves at a larger scale and how to optimize it, and measure real speed, memory use and learning with sforge-submit, which runs the full evaluation on hidden data. Keep notes in notes.md. Stop every GPU process before submitting with sforge-submit.

dual-cuda-sm90-nccl.notes: Qualified on two H100 NVL GPUs with 95830 MiB each; measured peak 84656 MiB (82.672 GiB) per card during Judge final evaluation. Floor 90 GiB leaves 7.328 GiB over the measured peak. Work and Judge serialize on the same leased pair. Reference uses CPU optimizer offload; see runtime/qualification.json.

dual-cuda-sm90-nccl-80g.notes: The 80 GB H100 SXM pair (NV18, 700 W; 81559 MiB per card). Qualified separately: runtime/qualification.dual-cuda-sm90-nccl-80g.json (reference T and scores; scores are comparable only within this profile). The SGLang engines' memory is a fixed fraction of the card.
